name: Cloud Firestore

dataTypes.when: Only if Firebase Authentication is also used and a user is signed in: every Firestore request then includes the Firebase Auth user ID.

ask: What user data does your app write to Firestore (names, emails, messages, photos/URLs, location, health, purchases...)? Declare each data type and its purpose; Firestore itself only stores what you send it.
Do you use Firebase Authentication together with Firestore? If no, remove Personal info / User IDs.
Can users delete the data you store in Firestore? This affects the deletion answers in the form.

sources.title: Prepare for Google Play's data disclosure requirements (Firebase)

notes: Automatically, the Firestore SDK only collects the Firebase user agent (device metadata, installer, SDK versions; 'never linked to a user or device identifier'), which has no matching Play data type. Everything else is developer-defined, so the real disclosure depends on what the app stores (see ask). Firebase's page does not give a per-product collected/shared table; it states globally that Firebase does not transfer the listed data to third parties except to subprocessors that help provide Firebase services or per the developer's instructions (e.g. linking to non-Firebase services). On that basis shared=false and role=service-provider. The page lists raw data items (e.g. 'stack traces', 'IP address'), not Play data-type labels; the mapping to Play labels and purposes here is ours.
